questions.question: Which process must crash in order for consensus to take at least 2 rounds?

answers.a: The process with the highest value/ID
answers.b: The process with the lowest value/ID

explanations.a: Incorrect: Crashing the highest value process does not necessarily delay consensus.
explanations.b: Correct: The process with the lowest value/ID must crash to force consensus to take at least 2 rounds.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Random crashes may not guarantee a delay of 2 rounds.
explanations.d: Incorrect: This scenario eliminates consensus rather than delays it.

questions.question: What happens when no processes crash during the consensus algorithm?

answers.a: Consensus is achieved in exactly f+1 rounds

explanations.a: Incorrect: Without failures, consensus can be achieved faster.
explanations.b: Correct: If no processes crash, all can broadcast in round 1 and consensus is achieved immediately.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Consensus is easier to achieve without failures.
explanations.d: Incorrect: The algorithm terminates when consensus is reached.

questions.question: In the fail-stop model, what characterizes a crashed process?

answers.a: It sends incorrect messages to other processes
answers.b: It stops executing and never restarts
answers.c: It continues running but ignores messages

explanations.a: Incorrect: This describes Byzantine behavior, not fail-stop.
explanations.b: Correct: A crashed process stops executing and never restarts in the fail-stop model.
explanations.c: Incorrect: A crashed process stops completely.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Message delays are not part of the fail-stop model.

questions.question: When must the lowest value/ID process crash for consensus to take at least 2 rounds?

answers.a: After it has broadcast its value in round 1
answers.b: Before it broadcasts its value to all processes in round 1
answers.c: At any point during the simulation
answers.d: Only after all processes reach consensus

explanations.a: Incorrect: Crashing after broadcasting will not affect the first round of consensus.
explanations.b: Correct: Crashing before broadcasting ensures other processes cannot receive the lowest value in round 1.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Timing of the crash is crucial to delaying consensus.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Crashes after consensus does not influence the rounds.

questions.question: What determines the final consensus value in the algorithm?

answers.a: The value of the process with the highest ID
answers.b: The average of all initial values
answers.c: The minimum value among all non-faulty processes
answers.d: The value of the last process to broadcast

explanations.a: Incorrect: The highest ID does not determine the consensus value.
explanations.b: Incorrect: The algorithm uses minimum, not average.
explanations.c: Correct: The consensus value is the minimum among all values from non-faulty processes.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Timing of broadcast does not determine the consensus value.

questions.question: Why does the algorithm guarantee that consensus will be reached in exactly f+1 rounds in the worst case?

answers.a: Because f processes will definitely crash
answers.b: Because there must be at least one round where all remaining processes broadcast
answers.c: Because the minimum value is always found in the last round
answers.d: Because Byzantine processes are eliminated after f rounds

explanations.a: Incorrect: Not all f processes need to crash.
explanations.b: Correct: In f+1 rounds, there must be at least one round where all non-faulty processes can broadcast.
explanations.c: Incorrect: The minimum value can be found earlier depending on crash patterns.
explanations.d: Incorrect: The algorithm assumes non-Byzantine processes.

questions.question: Which processes must crash in order for consensus to take at least 3 rounds?

answers.a: Only the process with the highest value
answers.b: The process with the lowest value first, and processes with lowest value in next round

explanations.a: Incorrect: Crashing only the highest value process does not delay consensus to 3 rounds.
explanations.b: Correct: The lowest value process and processed that received its message must crash to delay consensus to 3 rounds.
explanations.c: Incorrect: This is overly restrictive and does not align with the simulation observations.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Random crashes do not ensure the conditions for delayed consensus.

questions.question: What is the theoretical maximum number of rounds needed for consensus with n processes and f failures?

explanations.a: Incorrect: The algorithm requires one additional round beyond the maximum failures.
explanations.b: Correct: The algorithm guarantees consensus in at most f+1 rounds.
explanations.c: Incorrect: The number of rounds is not directly related to n.
explanations.d: Incorrect: This does not represent the correct bound.

questions.question: When should processes crash in the second round, in order for consensus to take 3 rounds?

answers.a: Processes with the lowest value, before they manage to send to all processes without the lowest value
answers.b: Any process can crash at any time to ensure consensus takes 3 rounds
answers.c: Processes with the highest value/ID, before they send to all processes
answers.d: One of the processes with the lowest value, before it sends to all processes without the lowest value

explanations.a: Correct: Crashing the lowest value processes before they send to all processes without the lowest value ensures consensus takes 3 rounds.
explanations.b: Incorrect: Random crashes will not necessarily delay consensus for 3 rounds.
explanations.c: Incorrect: Crashing the highest value processes does not delay consensus for 3 rounds.
explanations.d: Incorrect: Crashing one of the lowest value processes does not ensure consensus takes 3 rounds.
